gaps.construct: pattern[i] indexing a string by byte
gaps.description: The doc never says whether Text is bytes or characters or whether it can be indexed; `bytes of pattern` is invented to get a byte view.
No search-from-end operation on Text is shown; `last position of "*" in pattern` returning a maybe Position is invented. Using maybe is cleaner than Go's -1 sentinel.
No slicing form exists for Text or List; `slice of pattern from 0 until pos` is invented, reusing the doc's `until` range convention.
The doc has no character or byte literal, only double-quoted Text, so the single byte is written as a one-character Text.

gaps.construct: multiple return values (prefix, suffix string, err error)
gaps.description: Scribe has one result plus a failure channel, so the two strings need a helper record type declared just for this function.

gaps.construct: constructing a record value with named fields
gaps.description: The doc shows record construction only once (`an Order from cart and receipt with status Paid`) without a general rule; the `with field as value and field as value` form is borrowed from choice declarations.
`count of` on Text is not defined as bytes or characters.

invented_syntax: slice of pattern from 0 until pos
a Prefix_and_suffix with prefix as ... and suffix as ...
notes: The control flow is easy and reads better than Go (the -1 sentinel becomes a maybe that must be chosen on). All the friction is a missing Text and byte vocabulary: indexing, searching and slicing, which nearly every text-handling function needs. The doc should decide whether Text is a byte sequence, a code-point sequence, or opaque with explicit views.
